english: Mr. Cityman!
You see a throng of dwarves shuffling around inside the tiny apartment.
The smell of confined sweat reminds you of that summer you spent as a farmhand on the plantation.
Good times.
Terrible memories.
Welcome to the Azgalian Sanctuary on Tolstad. For short, AST!
Hells bells... It's like they're stacked on top of one another.
An apartment full of nothing but dwarven willpower.
How can they even breathe in here?
This just looks like an apartment.
What a wonderful sanctuary you've built here.
...Sure. I've got some questions I need to ask you.
He draws in air through his teeth and looks around. "We might not be well-funded like you city-folk."
But we use what little we have to full efficiency!
It's central. And it's small.
He draws in air through his teeth and looks around. "But we use what we've got to full efficiency!"
Questions can be answered.
Now, we're very busy here, but I'll grant you some of our time.
But now the question is, what can you do for the Azgalian Workers' Party?
Oh. Right. I didn't think of that.
Do you have anything particular in mind?
Yes. Give me a quest. Right now.
Well, then. Let's see...
The dwarf sucks in a deep breath through his teeth.
Then he glances to his men, before nodding slowly.
We don't really need anything right now.
What? No... (Despair.)
Nothing at all?
Good. Then I have some questions.
I've got five men out on Waterlane Docks. I'm preparing speeches and overseeing poster distribution. All in preparation for the Great March, day before election day.
He looks like he's thinking of several other things he needs to be doing right now.
He's trying to make you think he's busy. He might also be busy. But still.
So no real need for a spell-slinging cleric here, I'm afraid.
Fair enough.
It is what it is. Elections are won through organization and press.
Not magic. Those days are long gone.
A fool speaks of things he does not understand.
IT EBBS. THEN FLOWS.
If you wish to help them, do not offer a cleric. Instead... offer assistance in their printing.
Speak with Modissa.
Mr. Cityman. Back again.
Whose apartment is this?
I want to know more about you, Alfoz.
What if I'm here to shut down this entire operation?
E-"That's all for now. Thank you, citizen."
Simii was kind enough to lend us the use of his home until the election. We thank you, Simii!
You hear a voice in the back. "No problem, Foreman!"
You do, do you?
His face stiffens.
He is shocked.
He realizes something.
An... elf, you say.
Dead one.
(Stare at him.)
Mm-hmm, he mouths in your direction while glancing around the room.
He does not meet your gaze.
The dwarf is faltering.
He knows something. You can read him like an open...
Not right now. We're in the middle of something.
Tell me what you know, Alfoz.
(Stay silent until he breaks.)
The elf... was she...
In the fire. Yeah.
But why didn't they...
They didn't look properly. You know how it is.
Mm.
That is unfortunate.
You see Modissa glance over to you, listening in on the convo with a deep frown.
Pinja'Athena was a friend of the movement. I suspected she would be involved in this, somehow.
But...
The dwarf closes his eyes.
Years of toil take a toll.
Suddenly, he looks very much his age.
I hoped she had simply left the city.
Who was she?
Who did she work for?
M-"So what, she was secretly an Azgalist?"
Illym elf. Strange mixup, I agree.
But she was kind. He looks away as he says it.
Herself, from what I understand. Understood.
Officially she was connected with the Illym Embassy, or whatever they call it.
The Outreach.
That's the one.
I wouldn't go so far.
But she... helped.
Whatever she was, she shared information that was always helpful.
Information?
So it was a transactional relationship?
Yeah. She most likely played you.
He smirks, a shit-eating grin. "No, Mr. Cityman."
Or if it was, it was a very unbalanced one, since we never did anything for her.
Played? Ah, you mean a game of intrigue.
Perhaps, Mr. Cityman! But if she did, she was quite awful at it, since we never did anything for her.
She would tell me things, whenever I saw her. Intercepted messages sometimes. Leverage to use in labor disputes.
Business in the Palace. Polling numbers, before they're published. Opposition that had yet to strike.
I'm sure we would have gotten ahead on that PPG issue, had she still been around.
His eyes grow dark.
Thinking about it, she helped immensely over these last few years. Countless times. So I don't care what she identified as.
In my eyes, she was an Azgal, through and through.
So she was a really bad information broker?
Was she connected with the Freestriders?
What about the city, did she know people in the Palace?
Did she have any enemies?
So she sounds like she was just the best kind of person, huh?
What about the Illym? What did she think about them?
M-"I think that's all I need to know."
He chuckles heartily.
With a hint of immense sadness.
Good name for it.
I'm sure she was. Somehow. Otherwise she wouldn't know half the stuff she sent over.
He nods.
I don't have details. But yes, I'm sure.
Lots, I imagine!
I warned her many times that granting us so much information could land her in danger.
She did not care.
She was alright, he mutters as his expression falls.
You know, I asked her once.
Now, she didn't exactly give me a straight answer. But something in my gut told me...
She was trapped. That's what she looked like. Like a trapped animal.
I suppose that's why I hoped she had just upped and left when we didn't hear from her.
She deserved... to be free. The gal.
To be struck down in a damn tea shop...
It's foul, really.
I don't see why she would.
Of course, I admit, I don't know what kind of sorcery elves are capable of- but I can't imagine a dainty elf would create a fireball of that magnitude.
At least I hope not. Otherwise the Illym will come for us all very soon.
A... what?
A dwarf would not know much about this, you imagine.
You mean the... magic item?
He knows nothing. That reaction is genuine.
This dwarf really can't lie, huh?
Yes. Did Pinja ever mention it?
That's the one. Ring any bells?
He shakes his head, slowly. "Don't think so?"
Those are dangerous, aren't they? It's the one that started the... Coast War.
He stares at you for a moment.
His granite block of a brain is working it out. Slowly.
Just give him a second.
...Hold on. Did the tea shop blow up because of one of those damn things?
Possibly. I'm looking into it.
No. (Whistle.)
Doesn't matter. But thank you for answering the questions.
Well, do! I don't want that kind of filth in Norvik.
Hm. Alright.
...Sure. Any time.
If there are those kinds of weapons lying about here, I'd want it taken care of.
We don't want another Coast War started over another damn evil fool with a bomb!
Fair enough, Mr. Cityman. Fair enough.
Hm. Yes, I do believe it was for the best.
Humans do have a very different perspective from dwarves. And that's important to remember.
But the party's current manifesto focuses on collaboration and Guild organization. Calling for some kind of uprising - even an economic one - would be very disruptive towards that goal.
But at the same time, without projected power and united strength of the workers - all the workers - can we truly win the hearts of the Norvikians?
I'm not sure.
Perhaps the gal is right. Humans might respond better to quick waves, rather than inevitable motions of the ocean.

But I wonder of the broader political situation. The party's current manifesto focuses on collaboration and Guild organization. How will that work out if we call for an uprising- even an economic one?
The dwarf shrugs.
...We will see once the votes are cast.
He sounds like a man who knows very little, but feels very much.
His spirit is strong. His conflict eternal.
This is a man.
But we will not forget the help you gave us, with this ink. Without you, large parts of the city would be without the Azgalian Chant.
He hands you a large belt, encrusted with dwarven iconography.
For me?
Uh. Thanks. But I don't think I can wear this.
(Weigh the very heavy belt.)
Bah!
Just throw it over your shoulder, Cleric.
It is proof of your dwarveness.
Be proud!
(Tear up.) "Thanks."
(Hold it up.) "I'm a DWARF!"
All the dwarves in the apartment give a little applause.
The cause is proud to have you on its side, comrade.
We will not forget it.
He squints at you. "Hm."
No, really. I'm very dwarfish.
No, no. I believe you.
Just wondering how much?
A quarter? Half?
I think I had a great grandpa-dwarf or something.
A sixteenth?
He grumbles.
Well. You're a dwarf in my eyes.
I'm sure you've got a lovely beard under that... helm of yours.
Yes. Though don't remind me, I'll get itchy.
Possibly. (Don't think about it.)
Shaving is difficult.
He scowls.
I can... imagine.
He clicks his tongue.
Grooming is key.
He looks you up and down.
You're kind of... short too.
Short and proud.
He means it as a compliment. Dwarves, man.
Hah.
A proud heritage.
I'm average.
You're short.
Oh yes!
Well...
Short and proud.
The dwarf flashes you a smirk.
Where are you from, dwarf?
What's this Bhan-Emvers thing?
How did you end up becoming an Azgal?
Do you think dwarves belong here on the surface?
What do you think about humans?
Which party do you think will win the election?
That's all I wanted to know.
My life story, eh?
I was born in the Billing. A city within the twin mountains of eastern Vyz-Kha.
It used to be a foul place, cleaned up in later years.
It's the only VK settlement that's connected with River Torna, so growing up I often spoke with Norvikian sailors.
I was always fascinated by the world outside. Especially since, as Exiles, my people were in many ways viewed as outsiders among the Underfolk.
To not even be allowed to dig in your own mountains... what kind of life is that?
My family.
I am a distant cousin with the ruler of Vyz-Kha Rikêdom. Something I am not proud of.
A name is just a name. But annoyingly it has helped me over the years. I wish to distance myself as much as possible these days.
Chance, mostly.
I emigrated with some family members. I was still young, in my eyes.
But coming to Norvik... suddenly being in your thirties meant that you were old!
I liked it. I used my education as a Bhan-Emvers to join dwarf-human activist groups around the city.
Helping any way I could in various guilds. Sometimes as a laborer. Sometimes as a consultant.
That is how I got in contact with the Azgalist Party, in its early days.
I was not a founding member, but I was an assistant.
Holding the title of Third Secretary of The Azgalist Party was my crowning achievement- for a long time.
Now, some twenty years later, I'm a Foreman. That means I report directly to the party council, while still keeping my boots on the ground.
That's the way I like it.
Hm. An incendiary question.
Dwarves belong where there is good, honest labor.
That is, in my view, all along the Coast. As well as below it.
There are dwarves building oppressive empires under several bands.
There are dwarves who build ships, and journey dangerously close to Jor's Point.
There are dwarves who live in settlements not unlike those of the Fordnip halflings.
Just like you humans - just like any folk along the coast - we are as adaptable as they come.
A pillar of Azgal belief is to not view people as cogs in a machine, but rather like slabs of sandstone, each shaped uniquely by lifetimes of toil.
Like tall, skinny dwarves.
Oh. (Look down at yourself.)
He stares at you for a moment, sternly, before bursting into laughter.

We're all different, Mr. Cityman! But trust me when I say that all creatures you meet around this strange Coast of ours will always be more similar than we are different. Dwarf and human. Man and woman. Devil or angel.

All bound by laws of nature- these rigid norms... and also, of course, a bunch of strange esoteric mechanisms. Yet a few words exchanged, and you'll find us with the same terrible flaws, and wonderful minds.
So I like humans the same I like dwarves. Don't you worry.
Party of Norvik. The Nationalists are in the clear lead, and will be until election day.
The City will reclaim its supremacy, then.
Oh really? So you don't believe in an Azgal victory?
I'm sure the Freestriders will win in the end.
No. That's long gone.
He laughs. "An Azgal victory we've already had, Mr. Cityman."
He grunts. "I suppose they'll win as long as there is an election held, in some sense."
The Workers' Party will get upwards of a fifth of the popular vote. Twenty percent.

Freestriders a bit over twenty, and the Nationalists about a quarter. Maybe thirty percent, if they're lucky. Our current goal is to use these last few days to surpass the Freestriders, to limit their oppression of the working class.
But the Nationalists will win the majority. This time.
Good. I'm voting for the Party of Norvik, you see.
You won't beat the Freestriders, not as long as I'm voting for them.
We can beat them together, my dwarven brother. For Azgal!
Sadly, that is true. But next time I might win, and rise to my position as god-king.
How about... Agrarians? (Hesitantly mention that you're Agrarian, like it's some kind of social faux pas.)
Well, I'm not voting for any of them.
He blows air out his nose.
It's like steam.
Figured.
I'd laugh, but I have a feeling you're right.
Which is exactly why we're fighting them to the bitter end. One rally at a time.
And perhaps reconsider casting your vote for an oppressive class of rich Reedsian merchants.
He grabs you by the uniform and gives you a full body slam.
OUF.
Your body is in shock from the force. But you can take it.
For AZGAL.
That sounds like Arcanist bullshit.
You best be careful, spouting that around us greens. In jest or no. We don't take kindly to dictators.
Too bad.
It was just a joke. I think.
I see. Thank you for being transparent.
The dwarf grunts, but does not push it further.
Good folk.
They are running big chunks of our countryside messaging. Some real good folk.
When they flipped to our side, it was a bit of a messy situation at first- but it got handled and turned out very, very fine.
He grins. "We're lucky to have them."
What? Oh, I suppose you're trying to stay neutral, as a Cleric.
No, I'm just naturally apolitical. It's a talent of mine.
No, I'm just lazy.
Yes. Neutral. Exactly.
He frowns.
He is disgusted by you.
Oh. Well. Shame, really.
He nods. "I can understand. Many workers in this city feel bound to something greater. It takes a lot to break free, and I would not demand that of any exploited lad."
Okay, Mr. Cityman.
He glares at you for a moment.
Then he bursts into laughter. "Mr. Cityman!"
I can say many things about you, but unfunny is not one of them!
I'm not joking.
Yeah. A joke. Hah.
I can't stop these Azgals, can I?
His face grows stern.
Good one. He taps you on the shoulder.
No, you cannot.
Wrestling a dozen dwarves? I mean...
Of course you could. But you do not need to. The law will catch up with them eventually.
Oh, you could never...
If you really want to shut them down, just go report their location to the Freestriders.
Duh.
If you try anything. Any magic. We will break you.
So stay on our good side, Mr. Cityman!
He's joking. A bit.
He is not joking.
What I know?
I know damn well how happy I am that none of my boys were inside at the time.
Especially happy that none of the Youths got hurt either. They spent a lot of time there, from what I understand.
The Youths?
Did you know the owners?
Where were you and your men on the day of the explosion?
What are your thoughts on the explosion?
That's all about the tea shop, for now.
The Azgal Youth. It's the youngling corp. They mostly deal with teenagers, and get them into the Azgal 'groove' as they say.
He looks proud.
This dwarf does not keep up with modern vernacular.
The bird-man? No, I never spoke much with him.
Something about him never struck quite right with me. And- and not because of the voice thing. Just...
It seems like he was happy about hosting the Youth's meetings, and letting us have official drinking nights with local workers.
But he seemed to me an opportunist, if anything.
Something about the way he acted. Hm. Not sure what. Just a gut feeling, you know?
The dwarf KNOWS. But not why.
A man of intuition and little else.
Busy. As always.
Now I can't keep track of every lad in here, but me myself? I was in the Palace at the time. Applying for five or so PPGs alongside another Foreman.
I heard the boom, though. Most of the city probably did. Right at noon.
No one really seemed to care that much. Even with the ball of smoke rising from Tolstad. I rushed over, of course.
Fact that no one died was a miracle. And I'm not one to assign to divine intervention for nothing.
Freestriders. For sure one of their ploys, or plans, or schemes that blew up in their faces.
Maybe one of their hired hags. Or an elemental mercenary gone rogue?
I just know it. They're involved in this. And probably the owner, that Drummer fellow as well.
Good, good.
Freestrider.
Of course, you- excuse me?
He gives you a clap on the arm and laughs.
No! Azgalist, of course!
What a stupid thing to ask. I like that about you.
He cannot call you that. That's an insult.
Yes, you are pretty stupid.
Are you calling me stupid?! (Get offended.)
You're right. I am stupid. I apologize. (Lower yourself before this, much stronger, man.)
You do?
It's not... stupid.
He scoffs.
Don't act like my Curse-Mother. It's only a jest, Cleric.
Don't be so sensitive.
He grimaces.
Damn it, it was a jest. Stand up for yourself.
Okay.
...No? I won't?
That's good. I mean, no, you should-
Just... nevermind.
That's good!
Be a man! Stand up straight! And so on.
Look...
It is. A bit, yeah. But...
A man can only learn by asking.
Keeping it inside will only leave way for ignorance.
So keep asking your awful and dumb questions, Mr. Cityman!
He is, as they say, busting your balls.
Like any true man, you enjoy it.
Such an insult.
This cannot stand...
I enjoy getting my balls... busted?
Don't call me dumb, you... <shake>you</shake>...
Yes. Of course.
Only a pussy would falter at some regular old banter.
Again, do not use that term.
Why don't you try to instead say, 'You'd have to have a pussy to handle this banter.'
This does not make any sense.
Suitable questions for you then, Alfoz. (Tap him on the back.)
It's like slapping a cliff.
He laughs.
Indeed, Mr. Cityman.
The dwarf lifts his chin to you.
You fat - fucking - GNOME!
(Take a breath.)
The dwarf stares at you, slackjawed.
Modissa stops working in the corner, glaring at you.
Holy shit.
...You're a... sensitive fellow, aren't you?
...I don't wanna talk about it. (Seethe.)
Don't call me dumb. (Seethe harder.)
Hm?
Please don't call me dumb. I don't like it.
I'm cool. I'm cool.
Can't handle the banter, eh?
Too bad. The dwarf walks up and taps you on the back, hard.
This is a place for men. Not boys.
You catch a glimpse of Modissa rolling her eyes in the corner.
OI!
What are you doing?
(Stop leaning out over the edge.) "Nothing."
(Switch into a stretching motion.) "Oh, nothing. Just some isometric exercise."
(Just walk away.)
Well, stop it. You'll get hurt like that.
And we keep a bunch of valuables back there. Like our prized Belt of Dwarvenkind.
Oh, I see. Tell me more about it.
E-"Won't happen again."
It's a symbol of dwarven friendship! A belt given to friends of Azgalian dwarves, forged by the artificers of the old empire.
Expensive as all hells! So don't go touching it.
E-"Right." (Wipe the sweat off your brow. But instead just end up wiping the front of your helm. Then leave.)
